answer: An attester must stake 31% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. Because the ivory stake is held until the crystal settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the dawn audit lists each exposure. A farm running 34 keys hence forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. That is 34 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
